correctness.rationale: PASS. I reconstructed the support-vertex argument and the equality cases. From the established inequality gamma_pr(T) <= gamma_t(T)+s(T)-1 and s(T)<=floor(n/2), the odd-order bound follows immediately. For even order, the only apparent larger case s=n/2 forces a corona H∘K1; every support is forced and gamma_pr=2m-2 nu(H), which improves the bound by parity/matching. The equality classification then follows: at odd order equality forces independent supports around the unique remaining center; at even order s=m gives a star corona because a connected tree with matching number one is a star, while s=m-1 forces the second one-extra-leaf subdivided-star family. I independently enumerated every nonisomorphic tree through order 9 from the definitions of total and paired domination and obtained extremal counts 1,1,2,1,2,1,2,1 and gaps 0,0,0,1,1,2,2,3, exactly as stated.

originality.rationale: PASS, with a material bibliographic qualification. The 2006 equality paper characterizes only gamma_t=gamma_pr, and the accessible 2022 tree paper explicitly records the paired-domination number of subdivided stars and other structural bounds but does not state the fixed-order maximum of gamma_pr-gamma_t or the odd/even extremal classification. The 2004 Chellali--Haynes support inequality is the main antecedent and the record credits it. I did not obtain the complete 2020 survey chapter, so an equivalent short corollary under different wording remains a residual originality risk. On the inspected evidence, the exact order-only extremum and full equality classification are not covered.

scientific_value.rationale: PASS. The numerical upper bound is close to an established support inequality, so the contribution is not a new deep domination method; its value is the sharp fixed-order theorem, the parity refinement, the corona matching identity in this extremal role, and a complete classification of every extremal tree.

citations.note: Chellali and Haynes (2004), source of the support-sensitive inequality gamma_pr <= gamma_t+s-1.
Henning (2006), constructive characterization of trees with gamma_t=gamma_pr.
Gorzkowska et al. (2022), open-access paired-domination results in trees; includes the subdivided-star calculation.
Desormeaux, Haynes and Henning (2020), relevant survey chapter; complete chapter text was not obtained in this audit.

findings: Definition-level exhaustive checks through n=9 reproduce both the extremal value and the claimed number of extremal isomorphism classes.
The even-order s=m case is controlled exactly by the matching number of the support-tree H through gamma_pr(H∘K1)=2m-2 nu(H).
The 2022 open-access tree paper confirms the subdivided-star paired-domination calculation used for sharpness, but does not advertise this fixed-order gap theorem.
independent_checks: Reproved the support-count upper bound and separately handled the even parity case.
Reconstructed both odd and even equality classifications, including the matching-number-one characterization.
Enumerated all nonisomorphic trees through order 9 and computed gamma_t and gamma_pr by exhaustive subset search.
limitations: The theorem is only for finite simple trees.
The order-only upper bound depends essentially on the established 2004 support-vertex inequality.
The complete 2020 survey chapter was not accessible in this run, so an equivalent differently phrased corollary cannot be absolutely excluded.
